messages:
tara.nguyen: Hey team — ACME is seeing sporadic mismatched embedding dims from our embeddings endpoint. They send text that should produce 1536-d vectors but sometimes we return 768-d ones (and the client code treats it as a cache hit). Happens after yesterday's batching tweak. Repro snippet and request id attached: req=acme-req-20260310-42.

miguel.oliver: ugh. do we have the raw request headers + model name? that sounds like we might be accidentally keying cache w/o dim or using a shared prefix across model variants. can you paste sample req?

tara.nguyen: pasted below. note header x-tenant-id: acme, x-prefix: acme-ux-v2. body: ```json
{"input":"Update pricing for Q3","model":"openembed-large-1536","batch":true}
```
cache looks configured as `prefix:{tenant}:{prefix}:emb` on customer side. ACME says they didn't change anything client-side.

sam_support: pinging eng-ml and runtime. customer is hitting production and we've got billing noise bc of duplicate smaller vectors counting as new embeddings. they want an explanation or quick mitigation.

eng-bot: incident-bot created #inc-2026-03-10-embed-cache-dim with severity=low, sla=48h. suggested mitigation: set `embed_cache.strict_keying=true` for tenant if available.

miguel.oliver: quick check — could be that our batching code normalizes `model` string (aliasing) and we map `openembed-large-1536` -> `openembed-large` in key. if the cache key omits `dim` or `quantization` fields, variants collide.

tara.nguyen: logs from edge: ```
[2026-03-10T18:00:12Z] req=acme-req-20260310-42 key=acme:acme-ux-v2:openembed-large hash=abc123 dim=1536 hit=false
[2026-03-10T18:00:12Z] req=acme-req-20260310-42 batch_id=bn-7f key=acme:acme-ux-v2:openembed-large hash=abc123 dim=768 hit=true
```
so same hash, different dim and one path reports a hit.

kevin.runtime: that log pattern screams "prefix reuse across batching paths". two code paths: single-request fastpath -> builds key including `model` and `dim`. batching worker -> normalizes model -> omits `dim`. bug introduced in PR #4512 where batch key canonicalization was simplified.

miguel.oliver: can you repro locally? try creating synthetic parallel requests where first request stores 1536 vector then a batched worker returns a 768 vector from cache: steps: 1) send single request header x-prefix=acme-ux-v2 with model openembed-large-1536. 2) wait 10ms 3) send another request in a batch (same prefix) with model alias openembed-large. set `batch_window_ms=15` on the client.

tara.nguyen: I ran that in staging, reproduced consistently. repro curl commands: ```bash
# store 1536
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." -H "x-tenant-id: acme" -H "x-prefix: acme-ux-v2" -d '{"input":"test","model":"openembed-large-1536"}' https://inference.redwood/api/embeddings
# then rapid batched call that comes back 768 (simulate SDK batching)
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." -H "x-tenant-id: acme" -H "x-prefix: acme-ux-v2" -d '{"input":["test"],"model":"openembed-large"}' https://inference.redwood/api/embeddings
```

sam_support: customer-facing note: "we believe cache collisions across model aliases caused the mismatched dims. temporary mitigation: set `X-EMBED-STRICT: true` header on requests or disable SDK batching until we patch." want me to send?

miguel.oliver: yes please. also add `x-embed-dim: 1536` header as a stopgap — our cache key generator will include unknown headers if set. we'll push a quick internal flag to include `dim` in batched key.

kevin.runtime: timeline: revert PR #4512 on runtime (hotfix) -> redeploy batch workers to canary -> verify with ACME. If can't revert quickly, push config `embed_cache.strict_keying=true` for acme tenant. requires config change in tenant db + rolling config push. I can do the config change.

tara.nguyen: please do it and cc me. also customer asked about billing — since duplicates counted, can we credit the extra calls from window 18:00-19:00?

sam_support: raised billing ticket BT-889. set temporary credits and paused usage-based billing for that tenant for the hour.

miguel.oliver: dev note: PR to fix canonicalization should: include `dim` and `quant` flags in cache key; avoid reusing prefix-only keys; add unit test where two model variants generate distinct keys. sample new key pseudo: `md5(tenant + '|' + prefix + '|' + model_full + '|' + dim + '|' + quant + '|' + sha256(input))`.

kevin.runtime: deployed tenant config `embed_cache.strict_keying=true` to acme in prod at 2026-03-10T18:20:30Z. monitoring for cache hit/miss and dim mismatch alerts.

eng-bot: autotest-run started for PR #4680 (cache key fix).

tara.nguyen: ACME confirmed reduced incidents after 10 mins, still watching. thanks all. :pray:

sam_support: will follow up with postmortem and billing resolution once the PR merges.

miguel.oliver: followups for eng-ml: add telemetry metric `embed_cache.key_components` that emits which components were used when building keys. helps avoid silent regressions.

kevin.runtime: ack, adding to runtime sprint.

eng-bot: incident closed (severity=low) after tenant config fix and canary verification.
